topic: A person finds out their surprise party has been cancelled
text: I stepped into the house, the air felt different—lighter, perhaps. The scent of vanilla, usually my mom’s signal for a happy gathering, lingered faintly. But the house was quiet, too quiet. I checked my phone, no messages. The kitchen was spotless, a stark contrast to the usual parade of disposables and wrappers left over from party prep. Curiosity nudged me upstairs. My sister’s door was ajar, her room normally a fortress of secrets. Today, it whispered, "come in." She looked up, a flicker of something in her eyes. "So, um, about the party..." she started, trailing off. I smiled, a mix of emotions swirling but landing on the unexpected warmth of the moment. "It’s okay," I said. "Maybe next time." That day, I found a new kind of joy, in the quiet understanding between us.
